summary: The population-plan compiler resolves every derivation and gap locator against the retained bytes of its source under a declared row-numbering convention, and the acolyte states that convention.
why: E-0202: Core required a nonempty locator string and read it no further, so the reviewer of a row cell was the first thing in the path to compare a row:N:field with the row it names. E-0204 is the cost: an isolated producer numbered rows from 1 by physical line with the CSV header as line 1 and said so, the fixture and the review task number data rows from 0 with the header excluded, nobody had declared either, and under the task's convention 13 of 15 locators named a row past the end. The convention is now declared, row:N:field with N counting data rows from 0, a CSV header excluded and its names the fields, a JSONL non-empty line a row and its top-level keys the fields, field[i] element i of a JSON array; it is the one the fixtures already wrote. At admission the compiler parses the bytes retained under the named source, under the media type they carry, and refuses LOCATOR_NOT_RESOLVABLE with every miss in one detail. Resolution runs for text/csv and application/x-ndjson only: a reading declares neither, so a document capture's assertion locators stay the document adapter's to check. Values are never compared. Decision 27 in design/KNOWLEDGE_PACKS.md carries the whole ruling.
